name: Comfort Wear
palette: white, light grey, soft gradient or clean real-photo backgrounds. Text is black, deep navy or white. One accent color per ad (Comfort Wear purple #7A2FE0, royal blue or red) may color the KEY WORDS of the headline or fill solid blocks, bars, pills and offer circles with white text inside, as the brand's winning statics do. Accent-colored text is the exception, not the default: most headlines are black or white, and body copy is never purple.
font_style: heavy geometric sans-serif (Montserrat Black / Gotham Black / Poppins ExtraBold) or a bold condensed sans for headlines, set very large across nearly the full width, tight leading, 2 lines max; mix weights inside a headline for emphasis (e.g. 'Dear' regular, 'Nurses' bold); clean sans for small copy
prompt_rules: The shoe MUST be the exact shoe in the attached studio reference photo, unchanged: same colors, stretch-knit sock-style upper with pull tab, grid-of-small-squares pattern on the side panel, elastic bungee laces with a round toggle, double-chevron logo on the inner collar, chunky rocker midsole with a wavy side profile, lug outsole. Keep its proportions and every detail; only change its angle, lighting and setting as the layout requires. Do not invent a different shoe, logo or sole.

Show the shoe at its true, natural proportions, exactly like the reference photo: full length from toe to heel, natural height, roomy toe box. Never squash, flatten, shorten, stretch, compress or crop the shoe, and never render it smaller than its natural size relative to the person or scene.
This is a women's shoe: the person wearing it is always a woman (women's proportions and styling). Men may appear only as gift-givers or in the background, never wearing the shoe.
Render every word of on-image text exactly as written in quotes, spelled correctly, and no other text.

Add nothing the description doesn't ask for: no extra feature lists, icon callouts, price tags, badges, panels or captions. Never show other brands' logos or products; competitors appear as text names only.
High-end e-commerce photography quality, sharp focus, natural soft shadows, no watermarks, no extra logos.
Never add icon badges, SHOP NOW or other call-to-action buttons, logo lockups or a designed brand header to the image; keep it plain.
claims_to_avoid: 'orthopedic approved', 'podiatrist recommended', 'doctor recommended' or any cure/treatment claim
specific review counts or star ratings unless confirmed
fast/quick shipping speed or 'easy returns' wording (shipping and returns are top complaints); the approved offer stack below is fine

language_rules.es: All on-image text is in Spanish exactly as written in quotes, as a Spanish-speaking person living in the USA would say it (neutral US Latino, Mexican-leaning, using 'tú'). Keep every accent and sign: á é í ó ú ñ ¿ ¡. Numbers in US format (12,000 not 12.000; $59.95). Do not translate brand names. Use only the Spanish text given in quotes: do not add feature lists, icons with captions, price tags, badges or extra panels.

audience: Women only: the product is a women's shoe. Whoever wears the shoe in an ad is always a woman; men may appear only as gift-givers or background people, never wearing the product. Core buyers are 50-65+ (survey: 47% are 65+), so every word on the ad must be easy to read for older eyes.

format_guides.fb_comment: Render the testimonial as a real Facebook mobile comment thread, pixel-faithful to the current Facebook app: light grey rounded comment bubble on white, small round profile photo on the left (realistic woman matching the persona), commenter name in bold dark text (first name + last initial), comment text in Facebook's system sans font at normal comment size, a grey row under the bubble reading like "2d   Like   Reply", and a small overlapping reaction pill (like/love icons + a count) at the bubble's lower right. Optionally 2–3 stacked comments with replies indented. Plain, native, not designed; no Facebook logo.
format_guides.trustpilot: Render the testimonial as a real Trustpilot review card, faithful to Trustpilot's current design: white card with thin light-grey border, reviewer row with a small round initials avatar, reviewer first name + last initial and country code, a row of five green square star tiles with white stars (Trustpilot green #00B67A), a short bold review title, the review text in a clean sans font, and a small grey date. Show individual review cards only: no Trustpilot logo, no TrustScore, no overall rating or review count, no 'Verified' badge.
format_guides.x_post: Render as a real X (formerly Twitter) post screenshot, faithful to the current X app in light mode: white background, round profile photo top-left, display name in bold black, then grey @handle and "· 3h", the post text in X's Chirp-like sans at native size (black, left-aligned, no quotation marks), optionally an attached photo with rounded corners, then a grey engagement row with the reply, repost, like and view icons and small counts, all in X's thin grey icon style. No blue verification checkmark, no X logo, no 'Twitter' bird. It must read as a genuine X post, not a designed graphic.
format_guides.cartoon_3d: Render as a still frame from a modern 3D animated feature film: soft global illumination, rounded appealing character designs with expressive eyes, rich but tasteful color, cinematic depth of field, subsurface skin shading. Characters look stylized-cute, not realistic.
format_guides.comic_strip: Render as a modern webcomic strip: 3 or 4 panels with thin black borders and white gutters, clean confident ink outlines, flat colors with light shading, round speech bubbles containing exactly the quoted lines, simple expressive characters. Panel order reads left to right, top to bottom.
format_guides.flat_illustration: Render as a modern flat vector editorial illustration: simple geometric characters with minimal facial features, a limited 4–5 color palette from the brand colors, soft subtle grain texture, generous negative space, clean sans-serif type.
format_guides.claymation: Render as a stop-motion claymation still: characters and props sculpted from plasticine with visible fingerprint texture and slightly imperfect edges, handmade miniature set, warm soft studio lighting, shallow depth of field.
format_guides.retro_cartoon: Render as a 1930s rubber-hose cartoon still: black-and-white or sepia ink with one accent color, bendy limbs, pie-cut eyes, white gloves, wobbly hand-inked lines, vintage film grain and vignette, old-timey title card lettering.
format_guides.anime_soft: Render as a frame from a soft hand-painted anime film: lush painterly backgrounds, gentle watercolor light, clean line art for characters, warm nostalgic mood.

format_guides_note: Testimonial/review ads use fb_comment or trustpilot; tweet-style ads use x_post. Cartoon/animation formats (user rule, Oct 11: use them, both brands): cartoon_3d, comic_strip, flat_illustration, claymation, retro_cartoon, anime_soft. Aim for ~15–20% of every batch.

program.angle_rules: User rule 2026-10-13: the proven angles are healthcare workers (nurses), travel, teachers and overweight/plus-size women; mix and match them (e.g. a plus-size nurse, a teacher on a summer trip, a plus-size traveler). At least ~40% of every batch leads with a FOOT-PAIN problem in the customer's words, using the survey and review data (research/analysis.md section 9 and research/data/notion_angles.md): plantar fasciitis/heel pain (25% of survey), arthritis (11%), neuropathy (10%), bunions (7%), swollen feet, knee/back pain from standing, plus 'no diagnosis, just want comfort' (22%).

offer.rule: User rule 2026-10-13: ~30% of every batch are offer-style creatives showing the full stack (40% OFF, 30-DAY MONEY-BACK GUARANTEE, FREE SHIPPING) as the hero, in varied formats (offer tile, stamp/seal, sticky notes, receipt, shoe + big type, warehouse/last-chance). Mix offer statics into the winning angles (nurse, travel, teacher, plus-size) and foot-pain hooks.

program.layout_note: User rule 2026-10-23 (reconfirms 2026-10-18): ONE file per creative, 4:5 only. Render with `generate.py --layout feed` (the default); never `--layout native`/`extend`, no 9:16 file. Compose natively for 4:5 using the full frame. Shoes never look compressed. This overrides any older prompt text asking for native 9:16 + 4:5. Quality/budget: the user's 2026-10-13 budget rule (medium, ~$0.10-0.20 per ad) still applies unless told otherwise.
program.trend_research: User rule 2026-10-23: spend real effort on the Atria MCP/API for the NEWEST TRENDING STATIC formats every run, not just current/seasonal winners. Run `atria_pull.py inspo` (all inspo_queries) and `competitors`; sort by newest launch / fastest rank_delta_7d / most impressions; contact-sheet the image statics (`contact_sheet.py`), read every page, and write a short 'formats trending now' list (format name, who runs it, days running, what to borrow) into research/analysis.md. Net-new batches use at least 5 of these new formats (not 3); iteration batches take their big-swing formats from the same list. Name the trending source ad in based_on.

creative_rules_v2.rule: User rule 2026-10-26 (replaces the polished-ad look for new concepts). Fixes four issues in the test batches: (1) no features/benefits on the ad, (2) looks AI, not real, (3) offer too loud, (4) copy too clever. Set `"style": "ugc"` on a concept to apply generate.py's UGC rule and brand.json -> quality_bar_ugc; default for all new nurse/travel/Black Friday concepts.
creative_rules_v2.features: Every concept shows 3-4 plain feature/benefit labels (body part + benefit).
creative_rules_v2.real: Phone-photo / screenshot / handwritten-note look, real environments, real women 55+, imperfect framing. Native formats (fb_comment, trustpilot, x_post, text thread) are real UI. Illustrations only for the cartoon share.
creative_rules_v2.offer: One small line, sticker or handwritten note; never the hero. Standard: '40% OFF + FREE SHIPPING' and '30-DAY MONEY-BACK GUARANTEE' as one small line or two small stickers (exact words). Black Friday: one small tag, either '60% OFF SITEWIDE' or 'BUY 2 PAIRS, GET 2 FREE GIFTS' (3-pack cushioned socks + free travel bag), never both.
creative_rules_v2.copy: Headline max 7 words, everyday words, problem or benefit first. Patterns that win: '[Problem]?', 'Dear [Role], [benefit].', '[Outcome] in [number].', 'Built for [place/situation].', 'Say goodbye to [problem].', 'You'll forget you're wearing them.' Banned: wordplay, metaphors, props-as-jokes (permission slip, admit one, be the one who, lesson plan).
creative_rules_v2.proven_layouts: Two proven families (user feedback 2026-10-26 from an Atria MCP analysis, verified in our winners): (A) WINNING LAYOUT = white or very light background, ONE big shoe (35-60% of the frame), '12-hour shifts' (or the situation) in the headline, thin hand-drawn arrows to named conditions/features (Dear Nurses callouts, $229k at 4.34 ROAS; 12-hour shift list $858k). (B) SALE STATIC = same white layout showing three colors with the strike-through price '$90' crossed out next to '$59.95' (standard-offer weeks only; no prices in Black Friday week). Use (A) for about half of new concepts and the UGC look for the rest.
creative_rules_v2.avoid_designed_brand_look: Losing statics (e.g. May batches) were well-designed brand pieces: navy condensed headline lockup, icon badges, a SHOP NOW button inside the image. They read as ads and get ignored. Never add icon badges, CTA/SHOP NOW buttons, logo lockups or a designed brand header. Keep it plain: shoe, headline, arrows, small offer line.
creative_rules_v2.line_to_reuse: 'Your running shoes weren't made for 12-hour shifts. These were.' is a strong line that sat in a layout that got ignored: re-run it inside layout (A) (white, one big shoe, arrows).
creative_rules_v2.condition_naming: Name the conditions the winners name (plantar fasciitis, bunions, swollen feet) but as 'For plantar fasciitis' / 'Room for bunions' / 'Stretch fit for swollen feet' labels, not 'alleviates / heals / improves circulation' (claims_to_avoid: no cure or treatment claims). OPEN QUESTION for the user: use the winners' exact 'Alleviates Plantar Fasciitis / Helps with Hallux Valgus / Improves Blood Circulation' wording?

Arch support, cushioned heel, wide toe box, stretch-knit upper, slip-resistant grip, elastic no-tie laces

User: no need to fit all of it on one ad. Keep the Oct 26 rule: the lead offer is EITHER 60% OFF OR the buy-2 gifts, never both; free shipping & returns and the 30-day guarantee may appear as small supporting lines. 'Free shipping & returns' is the approved wording (never 'easy' or 'fast').

BLACK FRIDAY price boxes (user-provided 2026-10-27, for Q48_06): strikethrough "$120" -> sale price "$59.95". Note: $59.95 vs $120 is ~50% off, and the standing price claim is "$59.95 (was $90)"; confirm the reference price before running.
quality_bar: Match the quality of the brand's own top-performing ads (the benchmark image): polished commercial e-commerce production, crisp and bright, nothing that looks like generic AI stock art.
The shoe is the hero: it fills roughly 35-60% of the frame, sharp enough to see the knit texture, square pattern and bungee laces; often shown as a pair. Never a small shoe inside a wide scene.
Lifestyle shots crop tight on legs and feet (knee or mid-calf down), low camera angle, background softly blurred; faces are optional and never compete with the shoe.

Typography: one very large, heavy headline across nearly the full width, max 2 lines, high contrast, directly on a clean area of the image or on a solid shape. No translucent boxes, no drop-shadowed text over busy areas, no small headline.

Few elements: headline + product + at most 3 supporting elements (solid rounded pills, a solid offer block, or black hand-drawn curved arrows pointing at shoe features). Generous spacing, aligned edges.

Legibility for women 60+ (user rule 2026-10-13): all supporting text (feature/benefit labels, arrow callouts, pills, checklist rows, offer lines, comments) is large and bold enough to read on a phone at arm's length: at least about 1/25 of the canvas height per line (about 75px tall on the 9:16, 55px on the 4:5), high contrast, no light or thin weights, max 4-5 words per label. Use fewer, shorter labels rather than smaller text.

competitor_notes: Atria searches by keyword/domain, not brand name. Query by domain to find ads: hike-footwear.com, goclove.com (brand 'Clove'), hollowsocks.com, viasox.com, wearstand.com / 'WearStand' (STAND+). Snibbs has almost no data. Latest read: research/competitor_focus_2026-10-26.md and data/competitor_focus_2026-10-26.csv.
quality_bar_ugc: REAL, NOT AI (user rule 2026-10-26): the ad must read as a real phone photo, screenshot or hand-made note from a real customer or coworker, like the long-running competitor statics (Stepprs sticky notes on insoles, handwritten cardboard sign, selfie at a kitchen counter, hand holding the product, break-room and car-seat photos). No glossy studio render look.

The shoe is still the hero and clearly visible (about 30-50% of the frame), sharp enough to see the knit and square pattern, true natural proportions, worn on a real foot or held in a real hand or sitting in the real scene.

FEATURES AND BENEFITS are always on the image: 3 or 4 short plain labels tied to a body part or problem (for example Arch support, Cushioned heel, Wide toe box, Slip-resistant grip, Stretch-knit upper, No-tie laces), as arrow callouts on the shoe, a check list, or handwritten notes.

The OFFER is subtle: one small line, sticker or handwritten note in a corner or along the bottom edge, never a full-width block, circle or headline. Text stays readable (at least about 1/30 of the canvas height).
Headline is plain and direct: at most 7 words, everyday words, states the problem or the benefit. No wordplay, no metaphors. One headline plus labels, nothing else.
Legibility for women 60+: all supporting text large, bold, high contrast, max 4-5 words per label; fewer labels rather than smaller text.
